patient.chief_complaint: Progressive numbness and weakness in feet and hands over 18 months, worse in the morning
patient.history_present_illness: Gerald Whitmore is a 58-year-old accountant with a 16-year history of type 2 diabetes presenting with 18 months of progressive bilateral foot and hand numbness and weakness. He initially noticed burning discomfort in both feet that has evolved into dense numbness. He also notes increasing difficulty with fine motor tasks in both hands, particularly loosening jar lids, and has noted significant weakness when ascending stairs and rising from low chairs. He reports that the symptoms are distinctly worse in the morning with some looseness and improvement through the day — a pattern he has noted consistently. His diabetes was described as 'under good control' by his primary care physician with an HbA1c of 7.1% at his last check 6 months ago, and there has been no change in his diabetes medications. He does not take metformin (intolerant — GI side effects) and is on glipizide alone. B12 is therefore not a metformin-related concern. He denies alcohol use. He is on atorvastatin and has read online that statins can cause nerve problems, which he raises. Neurological examination reveals notable proximal weakness that he says has never been part of his prior neuropathy discussions. He is frustrated that two previous evaluations attributed symptoms to diabetic neuropathy without addressing the proximal weakness.

Neuropathy Workup.value: No M-spike; polyclonal IgG elevation 1,580 mg/dL

labs.interpretation: Abnormal values: Glucose 138 mg/dL (H), HbA1c 7.1 % (H), Fasting glucose (AM) 138 mg/dL (H), ESR 24 mm/hr (H), SPEP No M-spike; polyclonal IgG elevation 1,580 mg/dL (H), Rheumatoid Factor 128 IU/mL (H), Anti-CCP antibody 186 U/mL (H).

specialized_test.impression: ABNORMAL NCS/EMG — axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy with proximal involvement. Sensory and motor nerve amplitudes reduced in a length-dependent distribution; conduction velocities relatively preserved. EMG: active denervation and chronic reinnervation changes in distal and proximal lower extremity muscles, including proximal hip girdle sampling. Pattern indicates an axonal polyneuropathy with involvement extending beyond typical distal distribution

output.impression: Sural nerve biopsy: axonal degeneration, mildly reduced myelinated fiber density. No vasculitis. No significant perivascular inflammatory infiltrate. No amyloid deposits. Findings indicate an axonal neuropathy without evidence of vasculitis

X-ray bilateral hands and wrists: periarticular osteopenia at MCP joints bilaterally. Subtle joint space narrowing at bilateral 2nd-3rd MCP joints. No frank erosions on plain film. Findings early-moderate RA pattern. MRI hands recommended for erosion detection if clinical management requires.

output.interpretation: CSF analysis performed. See findings above.

output.impression: Targeted upper extremity NCS to evaluate carpal tunnel syndrome and cubital tunnel syndrome given hand symptoms. Results: No carpal tunnel syndrome (median palmar latency normal, no median-ulnar palmar latency difference). No cubital tunnel syndrome (ulnar motor across elbow velocity 52.8 m/s, normal). Findings consistent with diffuse polyneuropathy affecting hand intrinsics rather than focal entrapment.

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Rheumatoid arthritis-associated axonal peripheral neuropathy in a patient with comorbid type 2 diabetes

differential.key_features: 16 years of T2DM with HbA1c 7.1% — substantial contributor; differentiate from RA-driven pattern by progression rate and asymmetry.
Asymmetric or rapidly progressive features would shift toward vasculitis; need ANCA, complement, biopsy if asymmetric.
Routine screen needed; PPI/metformin can lower B12.
Atorvastatin neuropathy is controversial; mild, non-progressive typically.
Demyelinating features and proximal weakness on NCS would be needed.

optimal_actions.action: Order broad neuropathy labs (CBC, CMP, HbA1c, B12 + MMA, TSH, SPEP/IFE, urinalysis)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify reversible/treatable etiologies (diabetes, B12 deficiency, monoclonal gammopathy, thyroid disease)

optimal_actions.action: Order EMG/NCS to characterize axonal vs demyelinating pattern and distribution
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Length-dependent axonal vs demyelinating vs multifocal pattern; severity and distribution

optimal_actions.action: Search literature for DSP evaluation guidelines and etiology-specific recommendations
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Confirm AAN 2009 DSP workup, etiology-specific evaluations

optimal_actions.action: Review medications for neurotoxic agents and check interactions for symptomatic therapy
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Identify potentially neurotoxic drugs (chemotherapy, metronidazole, megadose B6, nitrofurantoin); guide neuropathic-pain pharmacotherapy

optimal_actions.action: Connective-tissue / vasculitis serologies (RF, anti-CCP, ANA, ANCA, ESR, CRP, complement)
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Document RA activity / exclude overlapping vasculitis

useless_tools.rationale: EEG is a cortical test and is non-contributory in peripheral nerve disease.
Head/brain CT has no role in peripheral neuropathy evaluation.
Brain MRI is not indicated in typical distal symmetric polyneuropathy without CNS signs.
Advanced cerebral imaging (PET/MRA/MRV/perfusion) has no routine role in peripheral neuropathy.
Echocardiography is not indicated unless cardiac amyloid is suspected.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated unless there is syncope or symptomatic dysautonomia with arrhythmia concern.

sequence_constraints.reason: Tier the workup — basic labs first, then targeted electrodiagnostic and tissue studies.

critical_actions: Differentiate axonal RA-associated neuropathy from concurrent diabetic neuropathy and vasculitis
Document RA disease activity (RF, anti-CCP, ESR/CRP) and screen for overlap vasculitis (ANCA, complement)
Optimize glycemic control given 16-year history of T2DM
Review medications (DMARDs, statins) for neurotoxic contributions
contraindicated_actions: Do not escalate immunosuppression without electrodiagnostic and serologic support for an inflammatory neuropathy
Do not attribute everything to diabetes without addressing RA activity
key_reasoning_points: Two plausible contributors (T2DM 16y and RA) — define dominant driver by NCS pattern and serology
Asymmetry, mononeuritis multiplex, or systemic features would shift toward vasculitic neuropathy
Routine B12 / MMA screen is required given comorbid PPI use

red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchor on residual radiculopathy as cause of leg symptoms
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Resolved disc herniation does not produce bilateral hand + foot length-dependent symptoms.

red_herrings.intended_effect: Premature statin discontinuation as putative cause
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Statin-related neuropathy is controversial and rarely the dominant cause; discontinue only if pattern fits and benefit-risk supports it.
